The closest match is SLATE, which evaluates AI-generated teaching slides by instructional effectiveness and learner knowledge acquisition, using a pretest-posttest design so gains reflect learning rather than prior recall [10]. It shows how to judge whether a provided text actually leads to learning, and reports near- vs far-transfer gaps and even negative learning gains for some systems [10].

If you mean learning new rules or preferences from text more generally, other papers focus on learning preferences from criteria or rankings rather than from instructional text: one learns evaluator preferences robustly under model mismatch [3], and another studies how LLMs can infer pairwise slate preferences for synthetic A/B testing [4].
